_comment: Reference points drawn on the record chart. Costs are in the contract's model: one hash unit per started 512-bit block of the input plus 192 overhead bits, one-time part only.

points.label: leanVM XMSS
points.note: The one-time signature under leanVM's XMSS: 42 chains of 128 bits with 3-bit chunks (7 steps each) and target sum 195, so 42·7 − 195 = 99 chain steps to verify (one block each with the 192 overhead bits); the leaf hash of the 42 chain ends (5376 + 192 bits) costs 11 blocks; the message encoding (704 + 192 bits) 2. The Merkle path (32 more) belongs to the many-time layer and is not counted. Lower bound: none was known (0).

points.label: This paper
points.note: A Verification Lower Bound for Hash-Based One-Time Signatures: 41 chains of length 20 hashed directly into the root verify every signature in 109 units (96 chain hashes, 11 blocks for the root, 2 for the index), proved secure in Lean; the lower bound 25 is proved in Lean (the two baselines of this site).
